name: Netherlands
sources: GDP $318.8bn and population 14.95m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series NLD, 1990 (318,799,003,994 and 14,951,510). This is the same series the rest of the roster's 1990 GDP figures sit on - USA 5980, Germany 1710, France 1270, Italy 1180, UK 1090, Spain 535 all match it - so the league table stays internally comparable.

Inflation 2.5%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, NLD 1990 = 2.454%. The guilder had been held at a fixed 1.1267 to the D-mark since 1983 and the Nederlandsche Bank followed the Bundesbank rate for rate; low German inflation was, quite literally, imported policy.

Policy rate 8.7%: three-month AIBOR interbank rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 8.682% (OECD Main Economic Indicators via FRED, IR3TIB01NLM156N). Above Germany's 0.07 by the small premium a follower currency pays even when the peg is credible.
Military 2.4% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), NLD 1990 = 2.369%.

Strength index 12: about 104,000 active personnel, 913 Leopard tanks in the 1st Netherlands Corps facing the North German Plain, and a blue-water escort navy of standardised frigates. Indexed below Italy's 26 and above Poland's 12-equivalent mass because the equipment is newer, and well below Germany's 38, whose corps this one fought beside and was a quarter the size of. NOT nuclear: the Volkel air base held United States B61 bombs under NATO nuclear sharing and Dutch F-16s were certified to deliver them, but the weapons were American property under American custody, and this field records possession.

Gross fixed capital formation 22.8% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, NLD 1990. The split into public 2.6% and private 20.2% uses the AMECO general-government gross fixed capital formation series; the private figure is the residual. CAVEAT: the total is transcribed from the World Bank series, but the public share is entered from reference knowledge of AMECO rather than re-read off it, and the split should be treated as the softest number in this file.

Revenue 41% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue including social security contributions, Netherlands 1990. High even by continental standards because the social insurance funds are financed by earmarked contributions that this measure counts.

Gross public debt 75% of GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP, NLD 1990 = 75.0%. Higher than Germany's 0.41 and France's 0.35, and one of the reasons the Lubbers cabinets spent the decade cutting.

Oil 0.07 mbd: Dutch crude production in 1990 ran under 80,000 barrels a day. This field UNDERSTATES the Dutch energy position badly and the schema is the reason: the Netherlands was the second-largest gas exporter in the world in 1990, producing some 70 billion cubic metres a year from Groningen alone, and there is no gas field in this record. Stated here rather than smuggled into oil_mbd as an energy-equivalent, which would be inventing.

Stability 82 and authoritarianism 0.08: set above Germany's 80 and France's 75. Consociational politics with no losers, three parties that have governed in every combination since 1945, no territorial question, and a September 1989 election that produced a working majority in nine weeks. There is no 1990 event in the Dutch record that a stability model should be marking down for.
Separatism 0.01: effectively none. The Frisian language has official status in Friesland and no political movement behind it. Below France's 0.03.

TFP trend 0.012: below Germany's 0.016. The Dutch record of the 1990s was an employment miracle, not a productivity one - the Wassenaar accord of 1982 traded wage restraint for working-time reduction and the decade's growth came from hours worked and from part-time entry, with labour productivity growth running below the German rate throughout. Entering Germany's number here would model the wrong miracle.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.5821%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series NLD (Netherlands): 14,424,211 in 1984 to 14,848,907 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 17 were held and are listed below with their citations; 31 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, comp_risc_superscalar, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. matl_semiconductor_lithography -> HELD (materials-manufacturing said held, semiconductors-computing said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Materials domain, materials-manufacturing).

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 5 cells: agri_tissue_culture_propagation (health and agriculture board), bio_monoclonal_antibody (health and agriculture board), bio_recombinant_pharma (health and agriculture board), core_pcr (health and agriculture board), ener_seismic_3d_imaging (energy and transport board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

granted.source: Route (b), inherited from comp_microprocessor: World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 9.35 PCs per 100. Corroborating production context: the European Investment Bank carries a 1988 project titled 'Philips Submicron Nijmegen' (project 19881700) financing submicron IC production installations at Nijmegen - I could not establish its production start date, so this grant rests on route (b), not on the fab.

CWI in Amsterdam established the first connection between Europe and the Internet on 17 November 1988, the first non-American organisation to gain access to NSFNET; CWI was already the central hub of the European EUnet network and its predecessor NLnet, ran the .nl registry from Piet Beertema's office, and in early 1989 spun its services out into Stichting NLnet, the first independent provider in the Netherlands. Domestic routing, domestic hosts, domestic administration - the predicate's exact terms.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Cornelissen MTE, van den Tweel JG, Struyk APHB, Jebbink MF et al., 'Localization of human papillomavirus type 16 DNA using the polymerase chain reaction in the cervix uteri of women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia', Journal of General Virology 1989;70(Pt 10):2555-62 (PMID 2552002), Department of Medical Microbiology, University of Amsterdam. Corroborated by 'Human papillomavirus detection in paraffin-embedded cervical carcinomas and metastases of the carcinomas by the polymerase chain reaction', American Journal of Pathology 1989 (PMID 2552814), whose affiliation is a DIAGNOSTIC CENTRE - Diagnostic Centre SSDZ, Department of Pathology, Delft - i.e. a service laboratory rather than a research institute, which is the better evidence of the two for a use-side claim. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 9.35 PCs per 100, 3.8x the World value of 2.45.
Oracle established a Netherlands subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above). The Netherlands also holds comp_microprocessor at 9.35 PCs per 100.
R3: the Dutch NMT-450 network opened in January 1985 (Nordic Mobile Telephone country launch record). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 79,000 Netherlands mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.
The Dutch NMT-450 network started up in January 1985 (Nordic Mobile Telephone country launch record). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 79,000 Netherlands mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

LIMB A FAILS and is not used - see this node's note; granted on the named-artefact bar. LIMB B: the Netherlands is in the Advanced Set. EVIDENCE E2, a named pre-1990 three-dimensional survey over this nation's acreage: the F3 block 3-D seismic survey in the Dutch sector of the North Sea, offshore the northern Netherlands, ACQUIRED IN 1987 over 384 square kilometres to identify the geological structures of the block and search for hydrocarbon reservoirs. Its acquisition year is unusually well attested for a 1980s survey because the volume itself is public: the Dutch government, through TNO, and dGB Earth Sciences released the F3 dataset, and it has since become the most widely reproduced 3-D seismic volume in the world, with 1987 stated consistently as its vintage across the literature that uses it (SEG Wiki, 'F3 Netherlands'; and the machine-learning and interpretation literature built on the same volume). LIMB C SEARCHED: no named, citable fact was found placing the Dutch North Sea sector outside 3-D acquisition before 1990. DISCLOSED LIMIT: as with the UK cell, this is one named dated survey, an existence claim rather than a claim about the share of Dutch acreage covered by 3-D on 1 January 1990.

Philips's half of the Megaproject was the 1 Mb static RAM, presented in 1987 - well past a million transistors on a six-transistor cell - produced in submicron CMOS at Nijmegen, and ASML had been shipping the PAS 2500 stepper since 1986.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Rongen-Westerlaken C, Wit JM, Drop SL, Otten BJ et al., 'Methionyl human growth hormone in Turner's syndrome', Archives of Disease in Childhood 1988;63(10):1211-7 (PMID 3196048), Department of Paediatrics, University Hospital for Children, Utrecht; and the same group's 'A controlled trial of methionyl growth hormone therapy in prepubertal children with short stature, subnormal growth rate and normal growth hormone response', Acta Paediatrica Scandinavica 1989 (PMID 2662700), and 'Effects of two years of methionyl growth hormone therapy in two dosage regimens', Journal of Pediatrics 1989 (PMID 2809902). TWO YEARS of methionyl (recombinant) hGH completed and reported by 1989 at a named Dutch university children's hospital. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Netherlands, 1990: 97%. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Netherlands,NLD,1990,97').

Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half. Philips Medical Systems at Best manufactured both modalities in the Netherlands through the 1980s — the Tomoscan computed-tomography series and the Gyroscan magnetic-resonance series — and Dutch teaching hospitals were among their first users.

NAMED-ARTEFACT BAR, CLASS E2: Haak HR, Weening JJ, Rischen-Vos J, Daha MR et al., 'Acute cellular rejection during effective early prophylactic OKT3 monoclonal antibody treatment after renal transplantation', Transplantation 1989;48(2):352-4 (PMID 2526973), Department of Nephrology, State University of Leiden. The phrase that carries the cell is EFFECTIVE EARLY PROPHYLACTIC treatment: prophylaxis is a standing protocol applied to every graft, not a trial of first use. A second Dutch centre, Department of Internal Medicine I, Erasmus University, Rotterdam, appears in the same 1986-89 OKT3 title literature. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.

INTIS (International Transport Information System), the Rotterdam port community system, was implemented in 1985 and operating in 1986. A. Long, 'Port Community Systems', World Customs Journal 3(1); Piernext (Port de Barcelona), 'The fourth wave of Port Community Systems'.

Commercial biological control in Dutch glasshouse vegetables: Koppert Biological Systems was founded in 1967 at Berkel en Rodenrijs and supplied Phytoseiulus persimilis against two-spotted spider mite and Encarsia formosa against glasshouse whitefly to Dutch tomato and cucumber growers through the 1970s and 1980s. LIMIT STATED: the founding date and the biological control agents are firm; the claim that this was the standard rather than a minority practice by 1 Jan 1990 is the weaker half of this cell. Note the Dutch Meerjarenplan Gewasbescherming, the obvious national-programme citation, dates from 1991 and is therefore NOT used here.

Dutch glasshouse horticulture centred on the Westland, with essentially all national tomato, cucumber, sweet-pepper and cut-flower production grown under glass. LIMIT STATED: the CBS glass-area series I could reach BRACKETS rather than pins 1990 - 10,520 ha in 2000, 10,550 ha in 2021, about 10,152 ha in 2023 - so this cell rests on the sector's continuity across that bracket and on the Westland's identity as a glasshouse district, not on a transcribed 1990 figure.

BUCKET C, NAMED-LABORATORY BAR. CLASS E1/E2: Pierik RLM, 'Commercial micropropagation in Western Europe and Israel', in Debergh PC & Zimmerman RH (eds), 'Micropropagation: Technology and Application', Kluwer Academic Publishers, 1990-91, pp. 155-167 (Wageningen University & Research publication record; AGRIS record NL9106017; Springer chapter DOI 10.1007/978-94-009-2075-0_9). The survey reports that in 1988 Western Europe had 248 COMMERCIAL tissue culture laboratories, of which 37 each produced more than one million plants a year, for a total West European production of 212.5 million plants; and that THE NETHERLANDS HELD 76 COMMERCIAL LABORATORIES AND PRODUCED 80 MILLION PLANTS IN 1989, its three largest crops being gerbera (17.1 million), lily (16.3 million) and Nephrolepis (14.4 million). Both survey years, 1988 and 1989, fall before the board. Seventy-six commercial laboratories is not a laboratory-scale or pilot activity; it is an industry, which is what section 1.3 requires. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found placing the Netherlands outside commercial micropropagation. LIMIT STATED, AND IT IS THE CELL I MOST WANT SOMEONE ELSE TO CLOSE: the same source names the Netherlands, France and Italy as the three largest West European producers, together 62% of production. I did NOT grant France or Italy, because I could not read the chapter itself and hold no per-country laboratory count or plant number for either; deriving their shares by subtracting the Dutch share from the combined one is my arithmetic and not the source's statement, and section 1.3 forbids exactly that. A reader with the Kluwer volume in hand should rule those two cells.
